# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

    subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"]
        F1["Pipes: |"]
        F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"]
        F3["Chaining: ; && ||"]
        F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"]
    end

    subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"]
        E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."]
        E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"]
        E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"]
    end

    subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"]
        C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"]
        C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"]
        C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"]
        C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"]
        C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"]
        C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"]
        C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"]
        C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"]
    end

    USE --> SAFETY
    SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN
    SAFETY --> EXAMPLES

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1188
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1188
- **Title**: fix(#1121): replay zero-byte watchdog-killed requests instead of dying aborted
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +334
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-02T12:31:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-02T12:44:33Z

## PR Description

## What & why

Bench run 36990604714 (post-#1125/#1127/#1129) still lost `gpt2-codegolf` + `polyglot-rust-c`: the FIRST provider request stalled, the run-idle watchdog fired, the run died `aborted: Request was aborted` with an agent.log of ~1.3KB and **zero `[net]` lines**. A task that never started must never kill the run.

## Root cause

The connect ladder (#1125) retries only inside `sendWatchedProviderRequest`, and only on `TimeoutException` from its own connect watchdog. When the ladder is still waiting (or the stall is the black-holed-endpoint case), the **run-idle watchdog** (`agent.dart _onRunWatchdogFired`) cancels the request token; the adapter translates the cancelled token into `StopReason.aborted` / "Request was aborted". That event reached `TransientRetryStream._drive` and hit the issue #1126 pre-commit rule: *first attempt + aborted = forward untouched*. No retry above the watchdog — the run ended aborted. The missing `[net]` lines were the same hole's second face: headless (`fa -p`) never wired `transientRetryNotice`, so bench artifacts could not distinguish "retried and survived" from "no retry layer at all".

## Design (one paragraph)

At the shared wrapper (`transientRetryStreamFunction`), the PRE-commit abort class now replays whenever **no one intends the abort**: a token cancelled with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` (the one machine cancel — latch re-armed in place via `CancelToken.reset`, per the #1132 discipline, so tool phases and later user aborts keep working on the SAME token) or a provider/gateway-emitted abort with a healthy token (the E5 incident class from the run 36742787166 addendum). A USER bare cancel still stands and post-commit failures keep the #290/#1126 stand-rule (no transcript duplication). Watchdog fires landing inside the retry sleep are absorbed the same way (the sleeper already races the token; machine cancel → reset → retry). The connect watchdog's exhaustion wording (`… timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)`) joins `isTransientNetworkError`, so a #1125 ladder exhaustion flows into this budget instead of dying as a raw error. `providerTimeoutsOverride` is untouched — the ladder reads the injected timeouts as before. Finally, `runHeadless` wires `[net]` exactly like the REPL boot.

## Verification

Worktree `ai/gh-1121` @ cc4cf6364; dart 3.13.4; `PUB_CACHE`-isolated.

- `dart test test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` → **+53: All tests passed!**
  - new regression group `issue #1121 - a zero-byte stall survives the run-idle watchdog`:
    - **the bench repro**: attempt 1 = zero bytes then watchdog-cancelled abort → replayed, `DoneEvent('recovered')`, latch re-armed, `[net]` notice fired — fails pre-fix (`Expected: <2> Actual: <1>`, terminal aborted);
    - watchdog kills EVERY attempt → bounded loud death: `failed after 3` error with the per-attempt abort story, latch re-armed (never a fake `aborted` → addresses the #1122 misclassification at the source);
    - USER bare cancel pre-commit still stands (no replay, token latched);
    - provider-emitted abort, healthy token, zero bytes → replays (E5);
    - watchdog fire inside the retry sleep → absorbed, replay proceeds;
    - connect-watchdog wording classified retryable.
- `dart analyze` on the 4 touched files → **No issues found!** (repo-wide 104 infos identical on unmodified origin/main).
- Full gate `dart test --exclude-tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --exclude-tags llm` → **8537 passed, 24 failed, 16 skipped**; all 24 are sandbox-environmental (live PTY, macOS kernel-mode sandbox, process-tree reaping) — each reproduces identically on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree in the same sandbox.
- `crap4dart analyze` (0.11.0, CI-pinned) → `Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold: 12.00)`.

Fixes #1121

Now — an important subtlety with the E5 class (provider-emitted abort with healthy token): `pushStreamErrorEvent` sets aborted only if `error is AbortedError || error is CancelledException || token.isCancelled`. AbortedError — what is that? Provider/gateway-emitted abort. OK.

Now let me think about the CRITICAL question I flagged earlier — **the race between the wrapper's replay and the run-idle watchdog's one-shot timer at the AGENT level**:

1. Watchdog fires at T=480s → `run.source.cancel(error)` → token latched with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` → provider request dies → adapter pushes aborted error → wrapper (pre-commit) withholds, `_TransientFailure` → `cancelToken.reset()` → sleep 5s → replay attempt.

2. Agent loop: during all this, the agent sees NO events (buffer withheld). The watchdog timer was one-shot and consumed; `_touchRunWatchdog` re-arms it on the next processed event — which happens only when the replayed attempt forwards events. So after replay, events flow → watchdog re-arms with a full fresh `runIdleTimeout`. Reasonable.

3. But — what if the replayed request ALSO stalls with zero bytes for the full 480s? The watchdog is NOT armed during that window (it fired once and was consumed; the next arm happens on the next event). Hmm wait — actually `_touchRunWatchdog` is called on EVERY `_processEvent` — but during the stalled replay, no events are processed... so the watchdog stays DISARMED for the entire second stall! The run could then hang FOREVER: attempt 2 stalls (black-holed endpoint, no connect watchdog trip? — no wait, the connect watchdog WOULD trip at 180s...).

Actually — wait. The connect watchdog (`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`, 180s) trips when no response HEADERS arrive in 180s. A black-holed endpoint trips it → `TimeoutException` → connect ladder retries → exhausts `providerConnectRetries` → rethrows → adapter wraps as error event with "(connect watchdog)" wording → now classified transient by the new regex → TransientRetryStream replays. So the stall resolves via the connect watchdog at 180s boundaries. The run-idle watchdog is only relevant when the request produces headers but no SSE bytes... or when the connect watchdog is disabled (providerTimeoutsOverride with a longer/zero timeout?).

Scenario for the idle watchdog firing twice: attempt 1 connects (headers arrive), then the endpoint goes silent mid-... no wait, mid-stream silence post-commit stands (#290 AC4). Pre-commit: headers arrived but zero SSE events? The headers arriving means `httpClient.send` completed; the connect watchdog is satisfied. Then the SSE stream produces nothing → idle watchdog fires at 480s → cancel → aborted error pre-commit (no visible content) → replay → attempt 2 connects, silent again → watchdog re-arm? NO — the watchdog timer was consumed and only re-arms on the next `_processEvent`, which requires an event from the agent loop... The wrapper withholds pre-commit events (StartEvent is buffered!). So during attempt 2's silence, NO events flow → the watchdog remains disarmed → attempt 2 can hang indefinitely IF the connect phase succeeds and then the endpoint streams nothing and never times out at the transport level.

Hmm, but wait — is that actually true? Let me re-check `_armRunWatchdog`/`_touchRunWatchdog`: `_processEvent` → `_touchRunWatchdog(event)` → `_armRunWatchdog()` (re-arms a fresh Timer on every event when no pending tool calls). So the watchdog re-arms on every event. Between events, there's a timer running. When it fires, it's consumed (`_runWatchdogTimer = null`, and the timer itself fired). So after the fire, until the NEXT event is processed, there's no timer → no second watchdog fire → a second indefinite stall is unwatched.

BUT — this "second stall unwatched" behavior: was it also true pre-fix? Pre-fix, the watchdog fired once and killed the run — the run ended. Post-fix, the run survives the first fire but a second consecutive silent attempt (in the rare header-success-then-silent case) hangs forever (no transport timeout for SSE idle? — actually there IS an idle/stream timeout: "the idle watchdog's own TimeoutException wording" mentioned in the retry file — 'stream idle timeout'? That's a provider-side stream idle watchdog in createSseIterator — "Mid-stream silence never re-enters here — the idle watchdog fires downstream in createSseIterator"). So the SSE iterator has its own idle timeout (provider-level). If the endpoint connects but sends no bytes, createSseIterator's idle timeout fires with a TimeoutException wording that deliberately does NOT match isTransientNetworkError (so it stands). Hmm — but that's a mid-stream/post-headers situation → post-commit or pre-commit?

The SSE idle timeout error: stopReason=error, wording "stream idle timeout"-ish → `_retryableWireFailure` → isTransientNetworkError → deliberately false (idle watchdog wording doesn't match). So pre-commit → `_replaysAttempt` → false → forwarded → run dies with error. OK — bounded. So no infinite hang: any silent endpoint eventually produces SOME error event (SSE idle timeout), which stands. The only infinite-hang risk would be a request that never returns anything at all — but the connect watchdog bounds that at 180s. So every stall path terminates. Good — no infinite hang introduced.

Now — the retry budget interplay: run-idle watchdog fires ONCE per armed window. After the wrapper replays, if attempt 2 is silent again pre-commit, the SSE/connect timeouts produce standing errors (not replayed — the watchdog didn't fire again since it wasn't re-armed). The run dies with a loud error. Bounded. This matches the PR's "watchdog kills EVERY attempt → bounded loud death" story only partially (that test loops the watchdog at the wrapper level). At the real agent level, the watchdog fires at most once per silent stretch. Fine.

Next — **the `ProviderStreamState.stopReason` after reset**. When the token is reset and the attempt replays, the wrapper creates a fresh inner call. No state carryover. OK.

Now — **the E5 class risk: provider-emitted abort pre-commit with healthy token now replays.** Is there any legitimate pre-commit aborted error that previously stood as terminal and whose replay breaks semantics? What about host teardown cancel (e.g., the app closing a session cancels with a reason)? Any non-RunIdleWatchdogFire reason stands. Healthy token + aborted = replay (E5). The one hazard: a provider that emits `StopReason.aborted` as a NORMAL end-of-stream marker pre-commit (some providers use "aborted" oddly). If a provider legitimately ends with aborted pre-commit, this PR now retries it 3× (adds ~2×5s + 3× request latency) before surfacing. Edge-case, acceptable, and gated by budget.

Confirmed: in headless mode, `writeln` → **stderr**. So the `[net]` line lands on stderr, and stdout keeps only assistant text / HEP / stream-json frames. The [net] wiring cannot corrupt machine-parseable stdout. ✓

Now, one thing to verify: the `wireServe` path (`_WireServeSilentCliIO`) — `runHeadless` is NOT used for wire-serve (runWireServeHost instead). And the wire-serve host — does it wire the notice? Not required by the ticket.

Now let me double-check `runHeadless`'s stream-json mode: `_writeHeadlessEventHeaders` — writes HEP/stream-json headers to STDOUT. The [net] goes to stderr. ✓

Now, remaining checks:

1. **Does the `_TransientFailure` reset also need to happen when `attempt >= maxAttempts`?** It does happen (reset before the check) — deliberate.

2. **`_drive`'s reset on a token the CALLER owns (run.source)** — the token is the agent run's source token. Reset re-opens it for everyone. Documented pattern from #1126 (already used in `_AbortedPartial` branch pre-PR). This PR extends reset usage to the pre-commit path — consistent.

3. **Test quality check** — the headless test: after `runHeadless` completes, it fires the hook. But `runHeadless` is called and the global hook persists after the run (never un-wired). In the test tearDown of that file: `transientRetryNotice = null` added. ✓

   However — the test fires the hook AFTER the run completed. It proves the hook is wired, not that it's wired before any retry could fire during the run. `_wireTransientRetryNotice()` is at the top of runHeadless, before `_cubeBootRestore()` and the session init — so pre-flight compaction (which can also hit transient errors) is covered. Good placement actually.

4. **The un-wiring**: `runHeadless` wires the global but the REPL `run()` also wires it. If a process runs headless then... they're separate processes. The global is never reset to null on teardown — a test-isolation concern handled by tearDowns. In production, wiring twice is idempotent. OK.

5. **`zeroByteAbort` test helper race**: `scheduleMicrotask(() { scheduleMicrotask(() => source.cancel(...)); source.token.onCancel.then(...) })` — the inner `scheduleMicrotask` runs BEFORE the `.then` registration? Order: outer microtask runs → schedules cancel-microtask (M1) → registers onCancel listener (adds listener synchronously since not yet cancelled). Then M1 runs → cancel → listeners scheduled → listener pushes aborted. Deterministic. ✓

6. **Missing test: post-commit watchdog-cancelled abort** → `_AbortedPartial` path with watchdog — pre-existing behavior (#1126), tests exist presumably. Not this PR's scope.

7. **Missing test coverage**: the PR's `_replaysAttempt` change removed the `resuming` gate — the E5 test covers provider-abort-healthy-token on attempt 1 (non-resume). What about provider-emitted abort pre-commit with healthy token in RESUME mode? Same behavior. Fine.

8. Now a deeper one — **`_resumableAbort` with `cancelToken == null` returns true**: pre-PR, on attempt 1 with no token, an aborted event stood (forwarded). Post-PR it replays. If some provider emits aborted pre-commit as its NORMAL terminal (e.g. a proxy that aborts when client disconnects...), the wrapper now eats it and retries. Edge case, bounded by budget. Acceptable per design.

9. **`connect watchdog` in `_transientNetworkPatterns` — placement before the truncation class**: fine.

10. **The assertion in `_drive`: `if (cancelToken?.cancelReason is RunIdleWatchdogFire)` — but the `_TransientFailure` may NOT have been caused by the cancel at all!** Scenario: attempt 1 fails with a genuine transient `SocketException` (replayable wire failure), and INDEPENDENTLY the watchdog fires while the attempt was running (480s of silence... but a SocketException usually arrives quickly). Sequence: attempt runs → watchdog fires mid-attempt (cancels token) → the request dies with SocketException (network error, not abort) → adapter pushes ErrorEvent(reason: error) because... `pushStreamErrorEvent`: `cancelToken?.isCancelled` → true → aborted! Actually the adapter classifies ANY failure while token cancelled as aborted. So the event would be aborted, not error. To get `_TransientFailure` with StopReason.error while token cancelled: the event would need `StopReason.error` explicitly. Possible: the connect ladder's `TimeoutException` rethrow racing a token cancel — `pushStreamErrorEvent` checks `cancelToken?.isCancelled` → aborted. So in practice, watchdog-cancelled requests surface as aborted. The reset in `_TransientFailure` for a `RunIdleWatchdogFire`-cancelled token is thus consistent: whenever the token is watchdog-latched and we're about to retry ANY transient failure, reset. Correct — otherwise the replayed attempt would start with a cancelled token and instantly abort at the top-of-loop guard... wait no — the top-of-loop guard is only reached after the sleep; the reset happens before the sleep. If reset did NOT happen, the sleeper (`token.onCancel`) would resolve false immediately (already cancelled → `onCancel` completes immediately) → `_pushAborted`. So the reset is what makes the replay happen at all. ✓

11. **One more potential correctness issue — the notice for watchdog-replayed attempts**: `transientRetryNotice?.call(attempt, maxAttempts, delay, _shortReason(error.errorMessage))` — for the aborted case, reason = "Request was aborted". The user sees "[net] connection lost (Request was aborted) — retrying in 5s (attempt 2/3)". The wording "connection lost (Request was aborted)" is a bit misleading — an abort is not a connection loss, and after this PR the message could reflect a watchdog replay. Cosmetic; the CLI side formats `'[net] connection lost ($reason)'`. A clearer reason tag ("run idle watchdog replay") would help bench diagnosis — the very thing this PR is about. This is a legitimate SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-lite: the [net] line is the diagnostic artifact the PR exists to produce, and "Request was aborted" doesn't say WHY (watchdog vs provider). The fa.log line has the same reason. Hmm — but the reason string comes from `_shortReason(error.errorMessage)` which IS "Request was aborted". Could be improved to include the watchdog context when `cancelReason is RunIdleWatchdogFire`. I'd file this as a SUGGESTION.

12. **Test file organization**: the new group is placed at the END of the test file (line 2059+), inside `void main()`. Let me verify the structure — the diff shows the group added before the final `}`. The `+}` at the end closes main. Looks fine.

13. **`test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart` helper `zeroByteAbort(CancelTokenSource source)`** — takes the source as a param; used with the same source the wrapper receives. ✓

14. Line count check — the repo has a 2800-line size gate mentioned for agent_cli files: agent_cli.dart is 2664 lines, +5 = fine (the gate applies per file; agent_cli.dart was under). ✓

15. **CRAP gate**: PR says Max CRAP 0.00 — fine.

16. **`_replaysAttempt` unused-param cleanup**: signature now `(ErrorEvent event, CancelToken? cancelToken)` — the `resuming` param removed; `_bufferedOutcome` call updated. No other callers (checked? `_replaysAttempt` used only in `_bufferedOutcome`). Let me verify with grep.

17. **Behavioral double-check on `_replaysAttempt` for the RESUME path**: pre-PR, `resuming && _resumableAbort(...)`; post-PR `_resumableAbort(...)` unconditionally. For the PRE-commit path with resume state (a resumed chain's attempt): abort with healthy token now replays — consistent.

Now, one thing I want to verify: **does `_drive`'s `_AbortedPartial` branch handle a watchdog-cancelled token when `attempt >= maxAttempts`?** Pre-existing code:
```dart
if (attempt >= maxAttempts) {
  out.push(_resumeEvent(ErrorEvent(reason: StopReason.aborted, error: snapshot), resume));

}
```
Terminal aborted with resume prefix. Token NOT reset here — pre-existing (the #1132 review decided that?). Hmm — actually wait: is that a problem? Post-commit exhaustion → terminal aborted event, token stays latched with RunIdleWatchdogFire. The run loop sees StopReason.aborted turn-end. That's the #1126 design — out of PR scope.

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1188
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1188
- **Title**: fix(#1121): replay zero-byte watchdog-killed requests instead of dying aborted
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +334
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-02T12:31:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-02T12:44:33Z

## PR Description

## What & why

Bench run 36990604714 (post-#1125/#1127/#1129) still lost `gpt2-codegolf` + `polyglot-rust-c`: the FIRST provider request stalled, the run-idle watchdog fired, the run died `aborted: Request was aborted` with an agent.log of ~1.3KB and **zero `[net]` lines**. A task that never started must never kill the run.

## Root cause

The connect ladder (#1125) retries only inside `sendWatchedProviderRequest`, and only on `TimeoutException` from its own connect watchdog. When the ladder is still waiting (or the stall is the black-holed-endpoint case), the **run-idle watchdog** (`agent.dart _onRunWatchdogFired`) cancels the request token; the adapter translates the cancelled token into `StopReason.aborted` / "Request was aborted". That event reached `TransientRetryStream._drive` and hit the issue #1126 pre-commit rule: *first attempt + aborted = forward untouched*. No retry above the watchdog — the run ended aborted. The missing `[net]` lines were the same hole's second face: headless (`fa -p`) never wired `transientRetryNotice`, so bench artifacts could not distinguish "retried and survived" from "no retry layer at all".

## Design (one paragraph)

At the shared wrapper (`transientRetryStreamFunction`), the PRE-commit abort class now replays whenever **no one intends the abort**: a token cancelled with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` (the one machine cancel — latch re-armed in place via `CancelToken.reset`, per the #1132 discipline, so tool phases and later user aborts keep working on the SAME token) or a provider/gateway-emitted abort with a healthy token (the E5 incident class from the run 36742787166 addendum). A USER bare cancel still stands and post-commit failures keep the #290/#1126 stand-rule (no transcript duplication). Watchdog fires landing inside the retry sleep are absorbed the same way (the sleeper already races the token; machine cancel → reset → retry). The connect watchdog's exhaustion wording (`… timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)`) joins `isTransientNetworkError`, so a #1125 ladder exhaustion flows into this budget instead of dying as a raw error. `providerTimeoutsOverride` is untouched — the ladder reads the injected timeouts as before. Finally, `runHeadless` wires `[net]` exactly like the REPL boot.

## Verification

Worktree `ai/gh-1121` @ cc4cf6364; dart 3.13.4; `PUB_CACHE`-isolated.

# pr-1188: fix(#1121): replay zero-byte watchdog-killed requests instead of dying aborted

## Description

## What & why

Bench run 36990604714 (post-#1125/#1127/#1129) still lost `gpt2-codegolf` + `polyglot-rust-c`: the FIRST provider request stalled, the run-idle watchdog fired, the run died `aborted: Request was aborted` with an agent.log of ~1.3KB and **zero `[net]` lines**. A task that never started must never kill the run.

## Root cause

The connect ladder (#1125) retries only inside `sendWatchedProviderRequest`, and only on `TimeoutException` from its own connect watchdog. When the ladder is still waiting (or the stall is the black-holed-endpoint case), the **run-idle watchdog** (`agent.dart _onRunWatchdogFired`) cancels the request token; the adapter translates the cancelled token into `StopReason.aborted` / "Request was aborted". That event reached `TransientRetryStream._drive` and hit the issue #1126 pre-commit rule: *first attempt + aborted = forward untouched*. No retry above the watchdog — the run ended aborted. The missing `[net]` lines were the same hole's second face: headless (`fa -p`) never wired `transientRetryNotice`, so bench artifacts could not distinguish "retried and survived" from "no retry layer at all".

## Design (one paragraph)

At the shared wrapper (`transientRetryStreamFunction`), the PRE-commit abort class now replays whenever **no one intends the abort**: a token cancelled with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` (the one machine cancel — latch re-armed in place via `CancelToken.reset`, per the #1132 discipline, so tool phases and later user aborts keep working on the SAME token) or a provider/gateway-emitted abort with a healthy token (the E5 incident class from the run 36742787166 addendum). A USER bare cancel still stands and post-commit failures keep the #290/#1126 stand-rule (no transcript duplication). Watchdog fires landing inside the retry sleep are absorbed the same way (the sleeper already races the token; machine cancel → reset → retry). The connect watchdog's exhaustion wording (`… timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)`) joins `isTransientNetworkError`, so a #1125 ladder exhaustion flows into this budget instead of dying as a raw error. `providerTimeoutsOverride` is untouched — the ladder reads the injected timeouts as before. Finally, `runHeadless` wires `[net]` exactly like the REPL boot.

## Verification

Worktree `ai/gh-1121` @ cc4cf6364; dart 3.13.4; `PUB_CACHE`-isolated.

- `dart test test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` → **+53: All tests passed!**
  - new regression group `issue #1121 - a zero-byte stall survives the run-idle watchdog`:
    - **the bench repro**: attempt 1 = zero bytes then watchdog-cancelled abort → replayed, `DoneEvent('recovered')`, latch re-armed, `[net]` notice fired — fails pre-fix (`Expected: <2> Actual: <1>`, terminal aborted);
    - watchdog kills EVERY attempt → bounded loud death: `failed after 3` error with the per-attempt abort story, latch re-armed (never a fake `aborted` → addresses the #1122 misclassification at the source);
    - USER bare cancel pre-commit still stands (no replay, token latched);
    - provider-emitted abort, healthy token, zero bytes → replays (E5);
    - watchdog fire inside the retry sleep → absorbed, replay proceeds;
    - connect-watchdog wording classified retryable.
- `dart analyze` on the 4 touched files → **No issues found!** (repo-wide 104 infos identical on unmodified origin/main).
- Full gate `dart test --exclude-tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --exclude-tags llm` → **8537 passed, 24 failed, 16 skipped**; all 24 are sandbox-environmental (live PTY, macOS kernel-mode sandbox, process-tree reaping) — each reproduces identically on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree in the same sandbox.
- `crap4dart analyze` (0.11.0, CI-pinned) → `Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold: 12.00)`.

Fixes #1121

5. **`zeroByteAbort` test helper race**: `scheduleMicrotask(() { scheduleMicrotask(() => source.cancel(...)); source.token.onCancel.then(...) })` — the inner `scheduleMicrotask` runs BEFORE the `.then` registration? Order: outer microtask runs → schedules cancel-microtask (M1) → registers onCancel listener (adds listener synchronously since not yet cancelled). Then M1 runs → cancel → listeners scheduled → listener pushes aborted. Deterministic. ✓

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1188
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1188
- **Title**: fix(#1121): replay zero-byte watchdog-killed requests instead of dying aborted
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1121` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +334
- **Deletions**: -15
- **Created**: 2026-10-02T12:31:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-02T12:44:33Z

## PR Description

## What & why

Bench run 36990604714 (post-#1125/#1127/#1129) still lost `gpt2-codegolf` + `polyglot-rust-c`: the FIRST provider request stalled, the run-idle watchdog fired, the run died `aborted: Request was aborted` with an agent.log of ~1.3KB and **zero `[net]` lines**. A task that never started must never kill the run.

## Root cause

The connect ladder (#1125) retries only inside `sendWatchedProviderRequest`, and only on `TimeoutException` from its own connect watchdog. When the ladder is still waiting (or the stall is the black-holed-endpoint case), the **run-idle watchdog** (`agent.dart _onRunWatchdogFired`) cancels the request token; the adapter translates the cancelled token into `StopReason.aborted` / "Request was aborted". That event reached `TransientRetryStream._drive` and hit the issue #1126 pre-commit rule: *first attempt + aborted = forward untouched*. No retry above the watchdog — the run ended aborted. The missing `[net]` lines were the same hole's second face: headless (`fa -p`) never wired `transientRetryNotice`, so bench artifacts could not distinguish "retried and survived" from "no retry layer at all".

## Design (one paragraph)

At the shared wrapper (`transientRetryStreamFunction`), the PRE-commit abort class now replays whenever **no one intends the abort**: a token cancelled with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` (the one machine cancel — latch re-armed in place via `CancelToken.reset`, per the #1132 discipline, so tool phases and later user aborts keep working on the SAME token) or a provider/gateway-emitted abort with a healthy token (the E5 incident class from the run 36742787166 addendum). A USER bare cancel still stands and post-commit failures keep the #290/#1126 stand-rule (no transcript duplication). Watchdog fires landing inside the retry sleep are absorbed the same way (the sleeper already races the token; machine cancel → reset → retry). The connect watchdog's exhaustion wording (`… timed out: no response headers within 180s (connect watchdog)`) joins `isTransientNetworkError`, so a #1125 ladder exhaustion flows into this budget instead of dying as a raw error. `providerTimeoutsOverride` is untouched — the ladder reads the injected timeouts as before. Finally, `runHeadless` wires `[net]` exactly like the REPL boot.

## Verification

Worktree `ai/gh-1121` @ cc4cf6364; dart 3.13.4; `PUB_CACHE`-isolated.

- `dart test test/providers/transient_retry_stream_test.dart test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart test/providers/connect_stall_retry_test.dart` → **+53: All tests passed!**
  - new regression group `issue #1121 - a zero-byte stall survives the run-idle watchdog`:
    - **the bench repro**: attempt 1 = zero bytes then watchdog-cancelled abort → replayed, `DoneEvent('recovered')`, latch re-armed, `[net]` notice fired — fails pre-fix (`Expected: <2> Actual: <1>`, terminal aborted);
    - watchdog kills EVERY attempt → bounded loud death: `failed after 3` error with the per-attempt abort story, latch re-armed (never a fake `aborted` → addresses the #1122 misclassification at the source);
    - USER bare cancel pre-commit still stands (no replay, token latched);
    - provider-emitted abort, healthy token, zero bytes → replays (E5);
    - watchdog fire inside the retry sleep → absorbed, replay proceeds;
    - connect-watchdog wording classified retryable.
- `dart analyze` on the 4 touched files → **No issues found!** (repo-wide 104 infos identical on unmodified origin/main).
- Full gate `dart test --exclude-tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext --exclude-tags llm` → **8537 passed, 24 failed, 16 skipped**; all 24 are sandbox-environmental (live PTY, macOS kernel-mode sandbox, process-tree reaping) — each reproduces identically on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree in the same sandbox.
- `crap4dart analyze` (0.11.0, CI-pinned) → `Max CRAP: 0.00 — OK (threshold: 12.00)`.

Fixes #1121

Now let me think about the CRITICAL question I flagged earlier — **the race between the wrapper's replay and the run-idle watchdog's one-shot timer at the AGENT level**:

1. Watchdog fires at T=480s → `run.source.cancel(error)` → token latched with `RunIdleWatchdogFire` → provider request dies → adapter pushes aborted error → wrapper (pre-commit) withholds, `_TransientFailure` → `cancelToken.reset()` → sleep 5s → replay attempt.

The watchdog timer was one-shot and consumed; `_touchRunWatchdog` re-arms it on the next processed event — which happens only when the replayed attempt forwards events. So after replay, events flow → watchdog re-arms with a full fresh `runIdleTimeout`. Reasonable.

The watchdog is NOT armed during that window (it fired once and was consumed; the next arm happens on the next event). Hmm wait — actually `_touchRunWatchdog` is called on EVERY `_processEvent` — but during the stalled replay, no events are processed... so the watchdog stays DISARMED for the entire second stall! The run could then hang FOREVER: attempt 2 stalls (black-holed endpoint, no connect watchdog trip? — no wait, the connect watchdog WOULD trip at 180s...).

Actually — wait. The connect watchdog (`effectiveProviderConnectTimeout`, 180s) trips when no response HEADERS arrive in 180s. A black-holed endpoint trips it → `TimeoutException` → connect ladder retries → exhausts `providerConnectRetries` → rethrows → adapter wraps as error event with "(connect watchdog)" wording → now classified transient by the new regex → TransientRetryStream replays. So the stall resolves via the connect watchdog at 180s boundaries. The run-idle watchdog is only relevant when the request produces headers but no SSE bytes... or when the connect watchdog is disabled (providerTimeoutsOverride with a longer/zero timeout?).

Scenario for the idle watchdog firing twice: attempt 1 connects (headers arrive), then the endpoint goes silent mid-... no wait, mid-stream silence post-commit stands (#290 AC4). Then the SSE stream produces nothing → idle watchdog fires at 480s → cancel → aborted error pre-commit (no visible content) → replay → attempt 2 connects, silent again → watchdog re-arm? So pre-commit → `_replaysAttempt` → false → forwarded → run dies with error. OK — bounded. 1. "connection lost" is factually wrong — the connection was killed locally by the run-idle watchdog, nothing was lost.
2. "Request was aborted" has historically meant USER intent on this surface. Post-PR the same string can now mean (a) watchdog replay or (b) a provider-emitted abort (E5) — a forensics reader cannot tell them apart, though the discriminator (`cancelToken?.cancelReason is RunIdleWatchdogFire`) is in scope exactly where the notice fires. The fa.log line inherits the same ambiguity.

Suggested fix at this site — name the machine trigger when it is the reason for the replay:

```dart

if (watchdogReplay) {
  cancelToken?.reset();
}
...
final reason = watchdogReplay
    ? 'run-idle watchdog replay of zero-byte request: '
        '${_shortReason(error.errorMessage)}'
    : _shortReason(error.errorMessage);
transientRetryNotice?.call(attempt, maxAttempts, delay, reason);
```

```

This pattern matches the human-readable wording produced ~600 lines away in `provider_common.dart` (`watchdogTimedOut()` → `… no response headers within ${…}s (connect watchdog)`). If that message is ever reworded, classification silently reverts to the pre-#1121 behavior.

// transient_retry_stream.dart
RegExp(RegExp.escape(connectWatchdogTag)),
```
```

Hmm — does `RegExp.escape` exist in Dart? Yes, `RegExp.escape(String)` static method exists. Good.

Comment 3 (SUGGESTION) — test ordering:

```markdown
💡 **SUGGESTION: the headless `[net]` test fires the hook after the run completes**

The test awaits `cli.runHeadless(...)` and only then invokes `transientRetryNotice`, asserting the output line. That proves the hook is wired at SOME point during `runHeadless`, but not that wiring happens BEFORE the first retry can fire: moving `_wireTransientRetryNotice()` below `_agent.prompt(...)` would still pass this test while reintroducing the exact #1121 blind spot for pre-flight-compaction and first-turn retries.

Firing the hook from inside the fake stream function (mid-run) would pin the ordering:

```dart

```

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

blocks.text:
# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane (live: fa pr-1104, 2026-09-30)

`chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs
may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a
factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride
the lane independently). Reviews must therefore:

- ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup,
  not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it
  from the release bump stranded the v1.0.494 tag behind the guest queue
  for an hour (fa pr-1104, unlabeled 13:31:08Z while pr-1105 was closed).
- ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via
  another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other
  PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours.
- ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review
  comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine
  only merges.

# GitHub tracker comment

Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue
comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every
construct must render natively on GitHub.

- Headings: `##`, `###`
- Bullets: `- item`
- Numbered lists: `1. item`
- Bold: `**text**`
- Inline code: `` `code` ``
- Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`dart`, `bash`, `json`)
- Link: `[text](url)`
- Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row)

Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks,
no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no
`{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on
GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable.

**IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues,
get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER`
(the composite key form works directly).
